payload.title: Separate human and MCP agent identity before enabling renewable staff login
payload.description:
## Intent

Keep a human newsroom session able to approve a delegation and a connected MCP agent able to perform already-authorized work. Start from the behavior in PPY-fdf150 and the implementation in PR #1244. This slice must land before a new Cognito audience can be trusted.

## Steps

1. Inventory audience and role checks in amplify/functions/shared/curation-caller.ts, its curation consumers, lib/newsroom-chat-identity.ts, amplify/site-backend.ts, and the AppSync and private Lambda tool boundaries. Add executable Gherkin first. Assert how current newsroom, CLI, IAM and Prospectus identities work.
2. Wire exact configured newsroom web, CLI agent and MCP agent client IDs from the backend that owns the user pool. Classify unknown or missing user-pool client claims as untrusted. A web client on an unseparated site retains its existing human permissions, and the existing unseparated agent delegation guard stays closed. Reject duplicated or incomplete client settings when renewable MCP is enabled.
3. Require the exact newsroom audience plus existing role checks for human-only delegation management. Preserve the explicit operator IAM lanes and their existing limitations. Keep CLI delegation semantics intact. Route MCP only through named typed operations and current review, delegation, publication, plugin and tenant gates. Record the same verified human actor plus the existing AI attribution.
4. Synthesize a site-opt-in, distinct public Google-only Cognito app client in the existing publication pool. Enable authorization code with S256, exact configured HTTPS /mcp/callback, rotation, 15-minute access/ID tokens and seven-day original refresh validity. Disable native, password, implicit, client-credentials and legacy REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH flows for this client. Keep the provider configuration and expected audiences trusted and server-side. Follow the site configuration, infrastructure review and release policy. Verify no unrelated clients change. Do not turn it on for a production site as part of this issue.
5. In local tests verify the provider adapter uses the exact configured pool, issuer, client, redirect and token uses, with matching signed subject, auth_time, nonce and verified staff groups. Keep the current documented shorter grant on sites with renewable MCP disabled. For the configured pilot, prove Cognito managed login can provide a fresh, verified authentication timestamp after the previous deadline. If the site/provider can't prove it, leave renewable MCP disabled there and record the failed proof.

## Gherkin acceptance

Feature: Distinguish delegated MCP actors from human approval
Scenario: A new agent client attempts a human-only operation
  Given a staff member has a verified MCP agent session and a delegation request
  When the agent attempts to approve its delegation
  Then the system refuses it
  And the member can still approve as a person through an authorized newsroom session

Scenario: A signed-in user presents a token from an unexpected client
  Given the token comes from the site's user pool and has an editor group
  When it names neither the newsroom nor a registered agent audience
  Then the curation gate denies it
  And no privileged operation is run

## Verification

Run focused curation and CLI identity tests, MCP OAuth Gherkin and hosting synthesis, then typecheck and the existing site/consumer build checks. Record the client and route review by identifiers only. Complete the actual provider proof on the isolated stable HTTPS pilot in PPY-17c201.
